segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ: ״גְּזַלְתִּיךָ״; ״הִלְוִיתַנִי״; ״הִפְקַדְתָּ אֶצְלִי, וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם הֶחְזַרְתִּי לָךְ אִם לֹא הֶחְזַרְתִּי לָךְ״ – חַיָּיב לְשַׁלֵּם. אֲבָל אִם אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם גְּזַלְתִּיךָ״; ״אִם הִלְוִיתַנִי״; ״אִם הִפְקַדְתָּ אֶצְלִי״ – פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּם.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who says to another: I robbed you,» or: «You lent me» money, or: «You deposited» an item «with me, and I do not know if I returned» your property «to you» or «if I did not return» it «to you,» he is «liable to pay» the sum or item in question. «But if he said to him: I do not know if I robbed you,» or: I do not know «if you lent me money,» or: I do not know «if you deposited» an item «with me,» he is «exempt from paying» the sum or item in question.

moves.summary: certain liability with doubtful return obligates; doubtful liability exempts

positions.claim: one who admits the liability but doubts return must pay; one who doubts the liability itself is exempt
